course.title: Agent Ops 101 — Agents, Autonomy & Operations in Production

modules.title: n8n: The Canvas as a Governance Surface
Apify: Real Data at the Input
The Learning Loop & the Living Course

objectives.text: Define agent operations and distinguish it from plain workflow automation with one test: does the system choose its own next action?
Name the six loop phases — notice, verify, decide, act, learn, report — and sketch the loop for one concrete product
State the operator's core question for any autonomous system: what did it do while nobody was watching?

lessons.title: The autonomy ladder: from chatbot to autonomous system

objectives.text: Place chatbot, copilot and autonomous systems on the autonomy ladder and say who initiates, who decides and who acts at each rung
Explain why authority must be earned by evidence and reversible by rule, not declared in a prompt
Read the PA0–PA3 authority ladder and predict which actions are permitted at each level
Map the six loop phases onto concrete components: actors, snapshots, the policy node, receipts, telemetry, the digest
Trace one real event end-to-end through the components and name the artifact each phase writes
List the four recurring failure classes — injection, drift, cost, silence — with one production example each
Argue why safety belongs in tested stop conditions, not in model politeness
Explain nodes, items, executions and credentials, and how data flows between nodes as an item array
Read an execution's recorded input and output for one node and say what makes it auditable
Choose between schedule, webhook and error triggers for a given job
Explain why an idempotent scan — dedupe on a content hash — is required before a schedule can be trusted

lessons.title: The Code node: deterministic decisions on the canvas

objectives.text: Write a Code-node rule block that decides an action deterministically, with no model call inside it
Explain why the decision belongs in code and the model only proposes answers to closed questions

lessons.title: Error workflows: a crash is never silence

objectives.text: Attach an error workflow to a production workflow and describe the payload it receives
Show how a thrown error becomes a receipt and a digest line instead of silence

lessons.title: Calling the world: HTTP, credentials & budgets

objectives.text: Configure an HTTP Request node with environment-variable credentials instead of pasted secrets
Set timeouts, retries and per-run caps for one external call, and say what happens when a cap is hit
Describe an actor's input schema, dataset, key-value store and run log, and the role of each
Say what a dataset row must minimally contain to be usable as evidence downstream

lessons.title: Running actors from n8n: pinning, waiting, paging

objectives.text: Run an actor from n8n and extract its dataset into items for downstream nodes
Justify pinning a specific build instead of `latest` in production, naming the failure the pin prevents
Apply the fetch → hash → cache order and explain what each step buys
Anchor a claim to a byte range in a cached snapshot so 'the source said this' stays checkable months later
Apply the two-independent-voices rule: two pages from one publisher count as one source
Recognise when a page is not evidence: single voice, stale, unreachable, or addressed to the operator

lessons.title: The two-stage judge: observe, then answer closed questions

objectives.text: Separate OBSERVE (extract candidate claims from a snapshot) from JUDGE (answer closed questions at temperature 0)
Explain why the judge never sees thresholds or the expected action, and what failure that design prevents

lessons.title: The POLICY node: ordered rules, first match wins

objectives.text: Order the policy rules R1–R8 and predict the action for a given input, first match wins
Explain parity testing: the same rules in JavaScript on the canvas and Python in tests, with zero disagreements allowed
Read a receipt: input, decision, reason codes, preserved quotes, artifact hash
Explain how a hash-chained receipt log makes an action arguable after the fact, and what verify_chain proves
Write a least-privilege tool permission block for one agent, host-scoped where applicable
Name the conditions that must stop the agent and bring in a human, and say why consent is one of them

lessons.title: Revert gates: publishing means promising to undo

objectives.text: Write a revert gate at publish time: metric, threshold, cohort minimum and deadline
Distinguish open, satisfied and unmeasured gates, and what each obliges the system to report
Define the two stuck signals — consecutive wrong answers ≥ 2, and dwell ≥ 3× the learner's median — and what each means
Explain consent-first storage: no consent row means nothing is stored, and the refusal is itself receipted
Write a micro-lesson to the fixed three-part contract — what it is, one worked example, one practice item — under the word cap
State the message caps (1 per learner per day, 3 per week, 1 per concept per 7 days) and why they live in code, not copy
Design a gold row and name the trap types an eval set must contain by name
Explain the three columns — proprietary one-shot, vanilla same-models, ours — and what column (b) proves about the rules
Apply the floor rule: below the gold-row floor nothing may be claimed except n and the legal degrade line

lessons.title: The morning digest: the system's face

objectives.text: List the five digest sections in fixed order and explain why refusals come first
Extract the operational facts from a real digest: mode, measured cadence, budgets, gate states and the unmeasured list

lessons.title: Costs, budgets & the discipline of units

objectives.text: Account for a run in the three currencies — tokens, actor units, and money (or an explicit unmeasured)
Configure a budget cap that escalates to a human instead of silently stopping the world

lessons.title: Capstone: run the loop on your own subject

objectives.text: Choose a moving subject whose sources are public, fetchable and independent, and justify the choice against the two-voices rule
Assemble the full loop — scan, triage, act, learn, digest — for that subject and name the artifact each phase leaves
Write the honest-degrade plan: what the system prints when the canvas, the actor or the judge is down

downstream_rule: Authored tree: a human revisits downstream lessons on edit, and the live loop (if it adopts this course) marks every lesson whose prereq chain includes a change as 'downstream to revisit' in the digest, never rewriting them in the same night.
